channel.description: Latest articles from Skeptics Society-Skeptic Magazine (skeptic.com)

item.title: Ufology: From Fringe to Mainstream to Fringe?
item.description: Former UK Ministry of Defence UFO investigator Nick Pope traces how ufology moved from conspiracy theory to Congressional hearings after the 2017 New York Times revelations. He then examines the infighting, whistleblowers, and quasi-religious narratives threatening to push it back to the fringe.

item.title: How Real Is the Nocebo Effect?
item.description: Can your mind make you sick? Carol Tavris dissects the “nocebo effect”—how negative expectations conjure real symptoms—separating genuinely startling science from anecdote and hype.

item.title: Where Have All the UFOs, Yeti, Demons, and Ghosts Gone?
item.description: Bigfoot vanished when everyone got HD cameras. Ghosts stopped appearing once smartphones arrived. UFOs avoid high-resolution lenses. This isn’t coincidence—it’s the most telling pattern in paranormal history. Why did supernatural phenomena disappear exactly when we could finally prove them real?

item.title: Martian Astronomers
item.description: Two astronomers, one legacy: Percival Lowell saw elaborate Martian canals that never existed, while Edward Barnard photographed the cosmos as it truly was. Their opposing approaches reveal how perception constructs reality—and why even honest observers can be utterly, spectacularly wrong.

item.title: Interstellar Interlopers: Anomalous Natural Objects or Extraterrestrial Technologies?
item.description: Three interstellar objects have drifted through our solar system, sparking debate between Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb, who suggests they could be alien technology, and scientists who see natural cosmic debris. Are these “interstellar interlopers” evidence of extraterrestrial life or just rocks?

item.title: Free Will Is Real
item.description: Is free will an illusion shaped by molecules and past events—or a real, emergent force within us? This mind-bending article uses philosophy, neuroscience, and cutting-edge science to argue that we are truly the authors of our actions. Free will is real—and provable.
